facts.statement: Prejanopterus lived during the Lower Cretaceous (lower Aptian age) in the Lezas Formation of La Rioja, Spain.
facts.quote: Prejanopterus is an extinct genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Lower Cretaceous (lower Aptian age) layers of the Lezas Formation of La Rioja, Spain.

facts.statement: A fossil site near Yacimiento de Fuente Amarga was discovered in 1980.
facts.quote: In 1980 a fossil site was discovered near Yacimiento de Fuente Amarga on the western slopes of the Peña Isasa.

facts.statement: Ten fossiliferous blocks containing pterosaur bones were recovered in 1993 and 1994.
facts.quote: In 1993 and 1994 ten fossiliferous blocks were recovered, containing numerous disarticulated fossil bones and bone fragments, among them those of a pterosaur.

facts.statement: The genus name Prejanopterus is derived from the village of Préjano and the Greek word for wing.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the village of Préjano and a Latinised Greek pteron, "wing".

facts.statement: The species name curvirostra refers to a claimed distinctive leftward bend in the snout.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from Latin curvus, "bent", and rostrum, "snout", a reference to the distinctive bend to the left which was claimed to be present in all fossils of the snout.

facts.statement: Later studies indicate the snout has a slight dorsal curvature rather than a sideways bend.
facts.quote: A later study indicates that "there is no genuine sideways bend" of the snout, "but a slight dorsal curvature".

facts.statement: The specific name was emended to curvirostris because the original feminine form was incorrect.
facts.quote: The same study emended the specific name to curvirostris as the feminine curvirostra had been incorrect.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen F. A. 112 consists of a fragmented snout.
facts.quote: The holotype, F. A. 112, consists of a fragmented snout.

facts.statement: Specimen F. A. 185, another snout, serves as the paratype.
facts.quote: Another snout, specimen F. A. 185, is the paratype.

facts.statement: All lower jaws found are remarkably straight.
facts.quote: Remarkably, all lower jaws found are straight.

facts.statement: While initially estimated at 4.26 meters, the wingspan is now thought to be no more than 2 meters.
facts.quote: The wing span was initially estimated at 4.26 m; however, later studies indicate that the wing span of Prejanopterus was probably not much (if ever) in excess of 2 m.

facts.statement: A 2012 study positioned Prejanopterus as a pterodactylid between the genus Pterodactylus and the group Ctenochasmatoidea.
facts.quote: In a later phylogenetic study Pereda-Suberbiola et al. (2012) recovered Prejanopterus as a pterodactylid, more precisely positioned between the genus Pterodactylus and the group Ctenochasmatoidea.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest Prejanopterus might be a lonchodectid based on its unusual tooth socket morphology and jaw shape.
facts.quote: Witton (2013) saw the genus as a possible lonchodectid due to its unusual tooth socket morphology and long, low nature of the jaw.

facts.statement: Prejanopterus lived between 121.4 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 119.57 million years ago)
